newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Hong Kong's Jardines plans big Taiwan expansion.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Jardines plans big Taiwan expansion.

text.p: Trading house Jardine Matheson, whose two centuries in Hong Kong bred deep suspicion in China, said on Wednesday it planned major new investments in another territory long estranged from China -- Taiwan.
"We have the idea to invest some T$12 billion (US$430 million) in Taiwan over the next three to five years," an executive at Jardine Matheson Holding Ltd in Taipei told Reuters by telephone.
"The exact amount will depend on the opportunity of the Taiwan market," he said.

The executive, requesting anonymity, said Jardines remained committed to Hong Kong and mainland China and that its interest in Taiwan should not be seen as a move away from Hong Kong on the eve of its July 1 return to China from British rule.
"Most of our assets are in Hong Kong. Even though our companies are registered in Bermuda or other places, we cannot run away from Hong Kong," he said.
Jardine Matheson Taiwan chairman Chang Liang said investing in Taiwan reflected nothing but good business sense.

"In order to diversify the group's risk, Jardine Matheson has selected several Asia-Pacific countries that enjoy high economic growth, such as the Philippines, Thailand and Taiwan, to undertake large-scale investments," Chang told Taipei's Commercial Times.
"The Taiwan market is especially seen as a major investment area," Chang told the newspaper in an interview.

It was not immediately known how Beijing would interpret a big Jardines expansion in Taiwan, seen by China as a renegade province since a 1949 civil war split left the island in the hands of the defeated Chinese Nationalists.
Jardines is no stranger to friction with China, which once branded the firm "the black sheep of business".

Prominent among Hong Kong's "hongs", or colonial trading houses, Jardines got its start in south China's notorious 19th-century opium trade, which led to war and Britain's seizure of Hong Kong island as a colony under the Treaty of Nanking in 1842.

Jardines angered China when it moved its domicile to Bermuda from Hong Kong in 1984 -- just after Beijing and London signed a pact agreeing to Hong Kong's 1997 return to Chinese rule. The move bolstered China's view of Jardines as a British partisan.
The group's companies were delisted from the Hong Kong stock exchange in 1994 and 1995, relisting in Singapore.
Jardine Matheson Holdings has deep links in Taiwan, pouring in some T$1-2 billion a year, the Taipei executive said.
The group's Taiwan operations include fast-food chain stores, supermarkets, furniture shops, shipping firms, real estate agencies and securities brokerages.
Jardine Matheson was considering investing in a supermarket joint-venture, a container cargo terminal as well as companies listed on the Taiwan stock exchange, the executive said.
He said the group was "very supportive" of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule, but that Jardines had global ambitions that went far beyond Hong Kong.
"We are an international company, not just a Hong Kong company," he said.
